questions.question: Bahu Mela in _________ is the major festival held at the Kali Temple in the Bahu Fort twice an year.

__
 
• **Bahu Mela** is a major festival held at the **Kali Temple** in the Bahu Fort.
 
• This festival is celebrated **twice a year** in the city of **Jammu**__.
 
• The Bahu Fort is a historical fort located in Jammu, which is a significant tourist attraction.
 
• The festival is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Kali, who is also known as **Bave Wali Mata** by the locals.
 
• During the festival, the temple and its surroundings are beautifully decorated, and a large number of devotees visit to seek blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Jammu** is known as the **City of Temples** due to its numerous temples and shrines.
 
• The **Bahu Fort** is believed to be one of the oldest forts in Jammu, built originally by Raja Bahulochan over 3,000 years ago.
 
• The fort has undergone several renovations and reconstructions over the centuries, particularly under the reign of the Dogra rulers.
 
• Besides the Kali Temple, the Bahu Fort complex also includes beautiful gardens known as **Bagh-e-Bahu**.
 
• The festival attracts not only locals but also tourists who are interested in experiencing the rich cultural heritage of Jammu.

questions.question: Which of the following articles lays down for protection from self-incrimination i.e. protection from standing trial against oneself?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 20**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 20** of the Indian Constitution provides protection against self-incrimination.
 
• It ensures that no person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves.
 
• This article includes provisions that safeguard individuals from being tried and punished more than once for the same offense (double jeopardy) and from retrospective criminal legislation.
 
• The protection under Article 20 is available to both citizens and non-citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 20(1)** states that no person shall be convicted of any offense except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offense.
 
• **Article 20(2)** ensures that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• **Article 20(3)** guarantees that no person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves.
 
• These protections are fundamental rights and form part of the basic structure of the Constitution, ensuring fair treatment in the judicial process.

questions.question: According to article 112 of Indian constitution, who shall cause in every financial year a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, the **President** shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, in respect of every financial year, a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India.
 
• This statement is commonly known as the **Annual Financial Statement** or the budget.
 
• The budget is a comprehensive statement that includes details on the revenue and expenditure, proposed allocations for different sectors, and the financial performance of the previous year.
 
• The budget is a crucial document for the economic planning and financial management of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• **The Union Budget** is prepared by the **Ministry of Finance** and presented by the Finance Minister in Parliament.
 
• **After the budget is presented, it must be approved by both Houses of Parliament before it can be implemented.**
 
• **The budgetary process includes debates, discussions, and voting on the budget proposals.**

questions.question: How many classical dance forms were officially acknowledged by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in India till 2023?

questions.question: Which of the following is defined as the number of females per thousand males in India?

• The **Sex Ratio** is defined as the number of females per thousand males in a population.
 
• In India, the sex ratio is a crucial demographic indicator that reflects the gender balance in the population.
 
• It is used to study the social and economic conditions of women in the country.
 
• The sex ratio can be influenced by various factors including cultural preferences, healthcare access, and policies.

• The sex ratio is an important measure for understanding **gender disparities** in a society.
 
• Government policies and social campaigns often aim to improve the sex ratio by addressing gender-based discrimination.

questions.question: Barabar Cave, famously known for depicting Ashokas' inscription, is situated at_______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jehanabad district**____**, Bihar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barabar Caves** are located in the Jehanabad district, near Gaya, Bihar.
 
• These caves are famous for their historical significance and the inscriptions of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• The caves were carved out during the Mauryan period in the 3rd century BC and are considered some of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India.
 
• They were used by the Ajivikas, a religious sect contemporary to Buddhism and Jainism.
 
• The inscriptions in the caves provide valuable insights into the history and culture of ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** was the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty and ruled almost the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• He is remembered for his contributions to the spread of Buddhism and his efforts to govern based on Buddhist principles.
 
• The **Barabar Caves** include four caves: Karan Chaupar, Lomas Rishi, Sudama, and Visvakarma.
 
• The **Lomas Rishi Cave** is particularly notable for its elaborate entrance which is an early example of the chaitya arch.
 
• The polished surfaces and precise architecture of these caves reflect the advanced engineering skills of the Mauryan period.
 
• These caves have inspired later rock-cut architecture in India.

questions.question: Which artificial element has been provisionally named seaborgium by American researchers in honour of Nobel Laureate Glenn T Seaborg?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Element 106**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Element 106** has been provisionally named seaborgium by American researchers in honour of Nobel Laureate Glenn T. Seaborg.
 
• Glenn T. Seaborg was an American chemist whose work in the synthesis of transuranium elements earned him the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1951.
 
• Seaborgium (Sg) is a synthetic element with the atomic number 106 and is part of the transactinide series.
 
• It was first created in 1974 by a team of researchers at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
 
• This naming honors Seaborg's significant contributions to chemistry, particularly in the discovery of ten elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seaborgium** is a radioactive element and does not occur naturally; it must be synthesized in a laboratory.
 
• It is part of the group 6 elements in the periodic table, which also includes chromium, molybdenum, and tungsten.
 
• The discovery of seaborgium was confirmed by both American and Russian teams, leading to international recognition of its name.
 
• Seaborg's work extended beyond element discovery; he also contributed to the understanding of nuclear reactions and the development of the actinide concept.
 
• The naming of seaborgium was unique because it was the first time an element was named after a living person.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating Body Mass Index (BMI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BMI = kg/m²**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BMI = kg/m²** is the correct formula for calculating Body Mass Index.
 
• BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women.
 
• The formula divides an individual's weight in kilograms by their height in meters squared.
 
• This measurement is used to categorize individuals into various weight categories such as underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obesity.
 
• BMI is widely used by healthcare professionals to assess the risk of diseases associated with excess body fat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) provides BMI cut-off points for categorizing individuals.
 
• A BMI of less than 18.5 is considered underweight, 18.5-24.9 is normal weight, 25-29.9 is overweight, and 30 or greater is obese.
 
• BMI does not directly measure body fat but correlates well with more direct measures of body fat.
 
• It is important to consider other factors such as muscle mass, bone density, and overall body composition when interpreting BMI results.
 
• BMI may not be accurate for all populations, including athletes and older adults, due to differences in muscle and fat distribution.

questions.question: Who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894?

• The IOC is the supreme authority of the worldwide Olympic movement.
 
• It was created to revive the ancient Olympic Games and to promote friendship and cooperation among nations through sports.
 
• Baron Pierre de Coubertin is often referred to as the father of the modern Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating every two years.

• The Olympic symbol consists of five interlocking rings, representing the five continents of the world united by Olympism.
 
• The Olympic Charter is the codification of the fundamental principles of Olympism, rules, and bylaws adopted by the IOC.

questions.question: As of April 2021, the ________ India scheme aims at providing people belonging to the scheduled caste or scheduled tribe or women of the country a loan between ₹10 lakhs to ₹1 crore, based on their requirement to promote entrepreneurship, which has been extended up to the year 2025.

• The scheme is designed to promote entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women, thereby encouraging them to start their own businesses.
 
• As of April 2021, the scheme has been extended up to the year 2025.
 
• The loans under this scheme are intended to help new entrepreneurs start greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or the trading sector.
 
• The scheme also offers support through the SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) for credit needs and other handholding services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The scheme is implemented through all Scheduled Commercial Banks in India.
 
• It is part of the broader financial inclusion strategy to ensure that the underrepresented groups get access to formal credit and contribute to economic growth.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the ocean floor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The deep sea shelf**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The deep sea shelf is NOT a recognized part of the ocean floor.
 
• The ocean floor is typically divided into different parts such as the continental shelf, continental slope, and the deep sea plain.
 
• The continental shelf is the extended perimeter of each continent, which is covered during interglacial periods by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
 
• The continental slope connects the continental shelf to the deep ocean floor.
 
• The deep sea plain, also known as the abyssal plain, is a flat, extensive area of the deep ocean floor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ocean floor is a complex and varied landscape with features such as mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, and trenches.
 
• Oceanographic studies and underwater exploration have revealed much about the structure and composition of the ocean floor.
 
• Technological advancements such as sonar mapping and submersible vehicles have significantly enhanced our understanding of the ocean's depths.
 
• The study of the ocean floor is crucial for understanding geological processes, marine ecosystems, and the impact of human activities on ocean environments.

questions.question: In 1883, which of the following allowed Indians to try Europeans in courts of law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ilbert Bill**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ilbert Bill** was introduced in 1883 during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Ripon.
 
• This bill sought to remove the racial discrimination inherent in the judicial system by allowing Indian judges to try European offenders.
 
• The bill faced severe opposition from the European community in India, leading to a compromise that diluted its original provisions.
 
• Despite its limited success, the Ilbert Bill marked an important step in the Indian struggle for equality and justice under colonial rule.

• The **Ilbert Bill Controversy** highlighted the racial tensions and the discriminatory practices prevalent in British India.
 
• Lord Ripon, who supported the bill, is often remembered for his progressive policies and efforts to promote local self-government in India.
 
• The controversy also spurred the formation of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885, which became the principal organization leading the Indian independence movement.
 
• The Ilbert Bill and its aftermath underscored the need for systemic reforms and greater Indian representation in the administration.
